classification_reasons: Blast radius is not small even though the spec is tight: the plan touches a brand-new module (plugin/lessons/index.py), a new gate check function registered in CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'], two command files, two templates, OPERATING_MODEL.md and a two-manifest version bump; the plan's own Risk 2 still names the gate check as the riskiest step because a wrong guard would silently stop enforcing the lesson/eval invariant for every future incident, not just fail loudly.

None of the touched code is covered by existing tests: plugin/lessons/index.py and the new lesson_and_eval check are new, with no prior coverage; the plan schedules new tests (test_lessons.py, new test_gate.py cases at a new phase-(e)-incident fixture, test_commands_and_skills.py extensions) rather than relying on anything that exists today.

The spec is now fully tight (every flagged concern closed with an explicit decision, including the reopened-and-reclosed Windows-newline concern, and the one remaining count mismatch between spec.md and plan.md from the prior round is now fixed), but tight-spec is only one of the three routine conditions; the other two (small blast radius, pre-existing test coverage) still fail, so the plan stays non-routine.
attempted: Intent: re-checked the current spec.md/plan.md against intent.md's Proposed outcome field-by-field; no scope drift from the fix round, and the two carried-forward open questions (sharing lessons across projects, eval-case frontmatter) are still correctly left to their named owners rather than answered here.

Spec and plan: confirmed the specific one-line inconsistency the prior verdict (at HEAD 065c4cf) flagged is now closed: spec.md's Acceptance bullet for the new gate check now enumerates the same seven fail cases as plan.md (missing lesson, missing a required frontmatter field, missing eval case, failing index.py check, a dangling supersedes, a supersedes target whose status did not actually move to retired, an out-of-enum status) in all three plan.md locations (Order of work step 2, the test_gate.py file item, Proof) and in spec.md Acceptance. Grepped both files for leftover 'sub-check'/'three new incident' language from the pre-fix draft (visible only in the historical removed lines of diff-b.patch) and found none in the final text -- the single lesson_and_eval-check framing is used consistently everywhere. Re-verified all 20 numbered requests in evidence/fix-requests.json against the current text one more time (gate guard ctx.status.entry_route=="incident" and ctx.phase=="e"; separate lesson_and_eval check with one CheckResult.need per line; (stale)/--today handling; README.md/index.md excluded by name from build; block-style/double-quote frontmatter rules; the reopened-and-reclosed Windows-newline concern with write_text(newline="\n")/universal-newline read/as_posix(); corrected runbook source; scan-filed-incident handling; corrected file:line citations (HANDOFF.md item 4 at line 42 vs item 11 for the frozen sample, test_gate.py fixture at 2306-2338 and the f-test at 2341-2354, docs/notes/1.md's flat frontmatter); plugin/lessons/__init__.py added to plan.md's file list; the misplaced 'No change to ...' paragraph moved out of the Files-that-change list into Risks; supersedes/retired_by wiring; allowed-tools additions; Risks 6/7/8 corrected and added) -- all 20 remain correctly applied, no regression introduced by the single-line fix commit.

Proof: no code exists yet at this phase (b is design-only); evidence/hook-log.jsonl shows only Edit/Write access to spec.md, plan.md and the adversarial-review-b.json evidence file across all sessions including the final edit at 15:41:25 (test_file_lock, protected_paths, secrets_check, format_on_edit all 'allow', no guardrail or source-file touches), consistent with a one-line design-phase fix; evidence/gate-b.json, claude-b.json and run-b.json are prior rounds' runner records and were read only for timeline context, never cited as evidence for or against this diff.

Blast radius: confirmed the diff touches only changes/0003.../{spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/*}; no file under .claude/**, this repository's own CLAUDE.md/REVIEW.md/sdlc.yaml, or any workflow template is touched; status.yaml's phase/gate fields are the change-folder's own tracking data, not a guardrail file.

Policies: data-conventions rules 1 and 3 remain correctly applied ('no risk_list item applies', 'no personal data'); template/sdlc.yaml and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md are still correctly treated as ordinary plugin content rather than this repository's own guardrails, per CLAUDE.md's guardrail list, and this phase's diff touches neither anyway (it only touches the change folder).

The tests: plan.md's fail-case list for the new gate check (seven, each tied to one line of rendered "what I need from you" text, now matching spec.md exactly) and test_lessons.py's planned coverage (ordering, Retired/Unsorted order, README.md/index.md exclusion, malformed frontmatter, zero lessons, (stale) with --today, CRLF check, class normalisation, a body line shaped like YAML to prove the frontmatter split stops at the second '---') each target a specific way the implementation could be wrong; this fix round touches no test file and change_type is 'feature', not 'fix', so the pre-existing-test-weakening rule does not apply.
